question.problem: Consider the Diophantine equation $3x+11y=7.$ The integer pair $(\overset{∼}{x},\overset{∼}{y})$ is the solution with the smallest possible positive value of $x.$ What is the value of $\overset{∼}{x}?$
question.worked_solution:
We have the linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

where $a=3,$ $b=11,$ and $c=7.$ We're given that the equation has solutions.

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(3,11)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}11 & = & 3\cdot 3 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 3 & = & 2\cdot 1 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =11-9 \\ 1 & =3-2\cdot 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =3-2\cdot 1 \\  & =3-(11-9) \\  & =3\cdot 4+11\cdot (-1).\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that $d=\text{gcd}(a,b)=1$ and

$$
3\cdot 4+11\cdot (-1)=1.
$$

Multiplying this equation by $7,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot 4+11\cdot (-1) & =1 \\ 3\cdot 4\cdot 7+11\cdot (-1)\cdot 7 & =7 \\ 3\cdot 28+11\cdot (-7) & =7,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that $(x,y)=(28,-7)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

$$
(28+\frac{b}{d}t,\,-7-\frac{a}{d}t)=(28+11t,\,-7-3t),
$$

where $t=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…\,.$

The smallest possible positive value of $x=28+11t$ is attained when $t=-2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\overset{∼}{x}=28+11\cdot (-2)=6.
$$
